summary: Glasgow Airport (GLA) is Scotland's busiest long-haul airport and the principal international gateway to the west of Scotland, located about 8 miles west of Glasgow city centre in Paisley, Renfrewshire. Originally opened as Renfrew Airport in 1933 and renamed Glasgow Airport in 1966, it serves as a major hub for airlines including easyJet, Jet2, Loganair, and TUI. The single-terminal facility underwent a major £31 million redevelopment completed in 2016, modernizing the departure lounge and check-in areas.
faqs:
Q: How far is Glasgow Airport from the city centre?
A: Glasgow Airport is approximately 8 miles (13 km) west of Glasgow city centre, typically a 20-30 minute drive depending on traffic on the M8 motorway.

Q: Does Glasgow Airport have a railway station?
A: No, Glasgow Airport does not have a direct rail connection. A planned Glasgow Airport Rail Link was cancelled in 2009 due to budget cuts, so passengers rely on buses, coaches, and taxis.

Q: Which airlines operate from Glasgow Airport?
A: Glasgow serves a mix of full-service and low-cost carriers including easyJet, Jet2, British Airways, Loganair, Ryanair, TUI, and Wizz Air, offering flights across Europe, North America, and holiday destinations.

Q: Is there a hotel at Glasgow Airport?
A: Yes, the on-site Holiday Inn Glasgow Airport is directly connected to the terminal, and several other hotels including a Travelodge and Premier Inn are located within a short shuttle ride.
transport_tips: The Glasgow Airport Express bus service (route 500) runs 24 hours a day between the airport and Glasgow city centre (Buchanan Bus Station) in around 25 minutes. The M8 motorway provides the main road access, though peak-time congestion can add significantly to journey times.
